note: Adapted from Sjöstedt's (1900) original description of Eutermes albotarsalis, which combines a Latin diagnosis with a German description; the queen is recorded only as similar to E. fungifaber with a total length of 25 mm and was not treated separately because the account is too brief; several figures, including wing length, wing width and soldier mandible length, could not be recovered from the damaged OCR and are not given; specimen records are not translated.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head reddish yellow or pale yellow, short rectangular, convex, broadly rounded laterally, posterior part broadly rounded, hemispherical in dorsal view, angles broadly rounded; frons obliquely truncate, rounded above and on both sides, slightly higher than the rest of the head; anteriorly with a fontanelle depression surrounded by fine hairs; below the depression a distinct gula; mandibles dark brown, rather stout, straight, incurved at the apex, distinctly shorter than the head; labrum slightly longer than wide, rectangular, slightly wider distally, with a deep median groove, almost truncate anteriorly, or with the anterior margin slightly oblique posteriorly from the middle; antennae 15-segmented, the cylindrical scape almost shorter than the two following segments together, the third segment smallest; pronotum oval, sides deflexed and constricted; anterior and posterior lobes equal in length, anterior lobe flat, very slightly emarginate in the middle; mesonotum about as wide, oval; metanotum wider, resembling an abdominal tergite; apical tarsal segment almost three times the sum of the remaining segments; head surface uneven, fish-scale-like, but overall smooth; body and legs almost smooth, hairs very sparse. Total length 7–8 mm, head with mandibles 4 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head white with a faint yellowish tinge, almost entirely smooth; clypeus inflated; frons as in E. fungifaber, with two larger and one smaller white circular translucent gland spots; first marginal tooth of the mandibles much larger than the others; antennae 15-segmented, the third segment smallest, white, gradually becoming brownish distally; pronotum oval, sides deflexed and constricted; anterior margin not emarginate in the middle; body white, filled with visible earth. Head width 1 mm.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Body dark brown above, head darker, deep chestnut brown; head slightly hairy, a little longer than wide, produced anteriorly into a triangular mandibular region, medium-sized, somewhat flattened, with a very small elongate fontanelle depression preceded by a small tubercle; frons with two small depressions; clypeus strongly convex, slightly paler than the frons, yellowish, truncate anteriorly, strongly curved posteriorly; first marginal tooth of the mandibles much larger than the others; compound eyes rather strongly protruding, ocelli circular, separated from the compound eye by about their own diameter; antennae 16-segmented, the scape about as long as the three following segments together, segments 1 and 4 about equal, segment 3 smallest, the remaining segments about equal in size, elongate-oval, slightly constricted at the base; pronotum almost as wide as the head between the compound eyes, slightly wider than long, nearly square, distinctly narrowed posteriorly; anterior corners rather short, slightly depressed, faintly concave; anterior margin straight, slightly reflexed; posterior margin wide, almost straight, slightly depressed and emarginate; above the margin a shallow arcuate transverse groove, and above the groove, in the middle, two small tubercles separated by a small groove; posterior margins of the meso- and metanotum each with two short pointed tubercles; wings rather broad, about 3 times as long as wide, dark brown with a slight reddish brown tinge; wing scales slightly wider than long, truncate apically; media fine, closer to the submedia than to the costa, with 2–4 (sometimes 5) branches at its apex; submedia running slightly above the convexity and then in a gentle arc to the posterior margin, giving off 10–11 branches; underside of the abdomen slightly paler brown than the dorsum, the first few segments pale in the middle, the last two almost uniformly dark brown in both sexes; membrane between the tergites and on the sides of the abdomen entirely white; legs pale yellowish brown, tibiae with dark shading; the first three tarsal segments white; apical segment about one and a half times the sum of the remaining segments; legs reaching the apex of the abdomen; abdominal appendages very small, wart-like. Wing expanse 28–32 mm, body with head 8–10 mm.
